name: Chicken Karahi
description: Chicken karahi with a concentrated tomato masala, fresh ginger and green chillies. Cook the chicken uncovered until the sauce clings to each piece, then finish with coriander.
ingredients: 1 kg bone-in chicken, cut into small pieces
1 tsp red chilli powder, or to taste
method: Pat the chicken dry. Heat the oil in a wide karahi or heavy frying pan over medium-high heat, then add the chicken in a single layer; work in batches if the pan is crowded. Brown for 7–9 minutes, turning once or twice.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and stir for a minute until fragrant. Mix in the chopped tomatoes, crushed coriander, chilli powder and salt.
Lower the heat to medium and cook uncovered for 15–20 minutes, stirring and pressing the tomatoes against the pan. If the masala sticks before the chicken is tender, add a small splash of water.

Continue cooking until the tomatoes have broken down, the chicken is cooked through and oil starts to appear at the edges of the thick sauce. Check the thickest piece; there should be no pink at the centre.
Add the slit green chillies and half the ginger. Cook for 2 more minutes, then taste and adjust the salt. Scatter the remaining ginger and fresh coriander over the karahi before serving with naan.
tips: Use a wide pan so the tomatoes reduce instead of steaming the chicken in a watery sauce.
Stir the masala regularly as it thickens; add water a tablespoon at a time if it starts to scorch.
Add the fresh ginger in two stages so some cooks into the gravy and some stays bright on top.
storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate covered for up to 2 days. Reheat until the chicken and gravy are piping hot throughout, adding a little water if needed.
serving: Serve hot with naan or chapati, sliced onion and lemon wedges.
